question: How does any object first appear in reflective awareness, whether inner or outer?
premises: Anything reflectively grasped may be inner or outer.
Such a thing first appears with its form not yet unfolded.
This initial appearance is described as shining forth.
inference: All reflective cognition begins with an initial, not-yet-unfolded appearance of its object.
uncertainties: The degree to which parimṛśyate implies deliberate reflection versus implicit awareness is interpretive.
plain_english: Here, whatever is reflectively grasped, whether within or without, first shines forth with its form not yet unfolded.
